captive_summary: The FSRU is one component of an integrated 'multi-phase gas-fired power complex and floating storage regasification unit (FSRU) terminal' developed by Energy Capital Vietnam (ECV) with B.Grimm Power, Siemens Energy and Gunvor International. The FSRU's function is to regasify LNG to fuel the co-located ~3,600 MW gas power plant (GOGPT's 'Ka Ga power station', 0.22 km away) — this is the direction-test relationship (terminal supplies the plant), not captive power to the terminal. No source found describes separate on-site/backup generation aboard or beside the FSRU itself.
confirmed_how: offshore-energy.biz (2019) describes ECV 'developing a multi-phase gas-fired power complex and floating storage regasification unit (FSRU) terminal' near Mui Ke Ga, Binh Thuan, with Siemens Energy supplying equipment to 'bring cleaner-burning gas' to the power complex. lngprime.com corroborates the $1.75bn FSRU-based project structure (ECV/B.Grimm/Korea Gas). Neither source, nor any other found, describes a separate on-site captive generator for the FSRU's own hotel/auxiliary load.
gogpt_prior_assessment: GOGPT's 'Ka Ga power station' (3,600 MW, tier C, 0.22 km) is the gas power plant this FSRU is designed to fuel, per the same ECV/B.Grimm/Siemens/Gunvor project sourcing above — it is the supplied plant, not this terminal's captive plant (direction test). See offshore-energy.biz above.
gogpt_candidate_basis: Existing GOGPT record already tracks the associated power plant (Ka Ga power station, tier C prior); it is a merchant/grid plant the terminal supplies, not a captive plant belonging to the terminal.
status_or_other_findings: GEM lists status 'shelved' (inferred 2y). Sourcing found dates to 2018-2019 (ECV/B.Grimm/Siemens partnership announcements); no more recent progress found in this pass, consistent with a stalled project.
notes: Direction-test case: FSRU regasifies LNG to fuel the co-located Ka Ga/Mui Ke Ga gas power plant — a PowerPlantsSupplied-type relationship, not captive. No vessel name found (vessel field blank in GEM data).

captive_summary: Genuinely early-stage proposed terminal (owner: ITECO JSC). Extensive Vietnamese- and English-language searching (by province, capacity, and owner name) turned up no independent public source describing this specific project's design, technical specifications, or power-supply arrangement. A separate, PV GAS-sponsored 'Trung tâm điện khí LNG' (LNG power center, ~3 Mtpa) proposal for Nam Dinh province surfaced in Vietnamese press, but its sponsor (PV GAS) does not match this record's owner (ITECO JSC) and could not be confirmed as the same project — not used as a citation here to avoid misattribution.
confirmed_how: No citable source found establishing captive power one way or the other for this specific ITECO JSC-owned record.
gogpt_prior_assessment: GOGPT prior 'Nam Dinh power station' (2,400 MW, tier B, 0 km) plausibly represents a co-located power plant this terminal would be designed to supply, mirroring the LNG-to-power bundle pattern seen at every other terminal in this shard, but this could not be independently confirmed from public sourcing in this pass.
gogpt_candidate_basis: Insufficient independent sourcing to confirm or rule out the terminal-plant relationship or any captive generation.
status_or_other_findings: None confirmed beyond GEM's existing 'proposed' status.
notes: Possible identity/conflation risk: a PV GAS-sponsored Nam Dinh LNG center project (3 Mtpa) is actively being promoted in Vietnamese press (2025-2026 dates) but under a different sponsor than this GEM record's owner (ITECO JSC) — flagging for reviewer to check whether these are the same or different projects; not acted on here.

captive_summary: Nghi Son LNG terminal is one integrated 68-ha site with the co-located ~1,500 MW Nghi Son gas-fired thermal power plant: 'the power plant, a warehouse, a regasification system, a wharf, and a ship anchoring zone' together in one project south of Nghi Son port, Thanh Hoa. The terminal's function is to fuel the power plant (direction test) — it is not captive power to the terminal. No source describes separate on-site generation for the terminal itself; the project remains pre-FID (repeated investor tenders, still seeking a developer).
confirmed_how: vir.com.vn ('$2.1 billion Nghi Son LNG-fired thermal power plant waits for investor') describes the integrated 68-ha site combining terminal and power plant. A second vir.com.vn article ('New life injected into idle ventures in LNG') corroborates the Nghi Son project's LNG-to-power structure and ongoing investor search.
gogpt_prior_assessment: GOGPT's 'LNG Nghi Son power station' (tier B, 0 km) is the plant this terminal is designed to fuel — direction test, not captive. Note: GOGPT lists 4,700 MW total for this plant while current (2026) press consistently cites 1,500 MW; flagging the discrepancy for the GOGPT side, not acting on it here.
gogpt_candidate_basis: Existing GOGPT record already tracks the associated power plant; it is the terminal's supplied plant, not a captive plant belonging to the terminal.
status_or_other_findings: Project remains pre-investment-decision as of 2026 (repeated tender rounds, most recently reopened per vir.com.vn); GEM's 'proposed' status is consistent with this.
notes: Direction-test case: PowerPlantsSupplied = Nghi Son Power Station (already noted in GEM data).

captive_summary: Early-stage greenfield terminal in Haiphong: Excelerate Energy and ITECO JSC signed a term sheet (Aug 2024) to co-develop, Phase 1 (0.7 Mtpa) targeted 2027, full capacity 1.2 Mtpa. Design is not yet finalized — one source notes Excelerate 'entered [a] partnership to study FSRU-based solutions' — no vessel has been assigned and no technical/environmental filing was found describing the terminal's own power supply. Excelerate's general newbuild FSRU fleet is known to carry dual-fuel diesel-electric auxiliary gensets (e.g. the H54DF model, ~9 MW), but this is fleet-level information, not confirmed for a specific vessel on this project, so it is not used to support a verdict here.
confirmed_how: vir.com.vn and theinvestor.vn confirm the Excelerate/ITECO term sheet and project scope but contain no power-supply detail for the terminal itself.
gogpt_prior_assessment: No GOGPT candidate plant given (gogpt_prior: no) — this terminal was not matched to a nearby GOGPT power station.
gogpt_candidate_basis: If the project proceeds as an FSRU (under active study), Excelerate's fleet-standard dual-fuel auxiliary gensets would likely make this a future captive-power YES with a citable nameplate — but at this stage there is no vessel, no filing, and no confirmed technology choice (FSRU vs onshore), so no GOGPT action is warranted yet.
status_or_other_findings: GEM lists both phases as 'shelved' (inferred 2y), but sourcing found (Aug 2024 Excelerate/ITECO term sheet, with subsequent coverage through 2025) describes the project as in active development, not shelved — flagging this status discrepancy for a future Update batch; not acted on here.
notes: Direction relationship not established — project is framed as serving northern Vietnam gas demand broadly, not explicitly bundled to one named adjacent power plant in sources found.

captive_summary: SCREENED: cancelled and never reached a captive-power design. Energy Capital Vietnam (ECV) relocated its LNG-to-power project from Bac Lieu (MOU only, no design work done there either) to Quang Nam in Nov 2018, commissioning a MODEC feasibility study for the Quang Nam site (expected complete Q2 2019). No subsequent technical/equipment design was ever published for Quang Nam. ECV's live LNG-to-power project today (per this same shard's Mui Ke Ga FSRU terminal — same sponsor, with B.Grimm/Siemens/Gunvor) is sited at Mui Ke Ga, Binh Thuan — a different location entirely, confirming Quang Nam was abandoned before design. GEM already carries this record as cancelled (inferred 4y), consistent with this finding.
confirmed_how: lngindustry.com and offshore-energy.biz (both Nov 2018) report ECV's move from Bac Lieu to Quang Nam and the MODEC feasibility-study commissioning; no later source found describing a completed design, permit, or equipment spec for the Quang Nam site, and ECV's currently active project (Mui Ke Ga) is a different, later site under the same sponsor.
gogpt_prior_assessment: No GOGPT candidate plant given (gogpt_prior: no).
gogpt_candidate_basis: Site never reached a design stage with power-generation specs; project was abandoned before any equipment/capacity was published for Quang Nam specifically.
status_or_other_findings: None beyond confirming GEM's existing cancelled/inferred status is well-supported.
notes: Same sponsor (ECV) subsequently relocated its live LNG-to-power project to Mui Ke Ga, Binh Thuan (see that terminal's entry in this shard).

captive_summary: Construction-stage (groundbreaking 18 May 2026) integrated LNG-to-power project in Nghe An developed by SK Innovation, PetroVietnam Power, and Nghe An Sugar (NASU). The 1,500 MW Quynh Lap plant and its LNG terminal are one project; SK Innovation is even exploring expanding the terminal into a 'hub terminal that supplies gas to nearby power plants' after construction — reinforcing that gas flows terminal-to-plant(s), not the reverse. No source found describes separate on-site backup/captive generation for the terminal itself.
confirmed_how: gasprocessingnews.com ('Petrovietnam Power, SK Innovation start building $2.2-B Vietnamese LNG power plant') and lngindustry.com ('SK Innovation breaks ground for LNG power project in Vietnam') both confirm the integrated terminal-plus-1,500MW-plant structure and May 2026 groundbreaking.
gogpt_prior_assessment: GOGPT's 'Quynh Lap power station' (1,500 MW, tier C, 2.28 km) is the plant this terminal supplies (direction test), not a captive plant belonging to the terminal.
gogpt_candidate_basis: Existing GOGPT record already tracks the associated power plant; it is the terminal's supplied plant, not captive to it.
status_or_other_findings: Construction confirmed via May 2026 groundbreaking, consistent with GEM's current 'construction/actual' status for this terminal — no status discrepancy found.
notes: Direction-test case: PowerPlantsSupplied = Quynh Lap power station (already noted in GEM data). SK Innovation is reportedly considering a future 'hub' role supplying additional nearby plants — still a supply-out relationship, not captive.

This is the direction-test relationship (terminal supplies the plants), not captive power to the terminal. A dedicated search for the project's ĐTM (environmental impact assessment) also turned up no mention of on-site backup/captive generation for the terminal itself.
confirmed_how: AES's own newsroom release ('AES and PV Gas Sign Joint Venture Agreement...Son My LNG Terminal') states the terminal-plant pairing directly (primary/operator source). lngprime.com corroborates the AES/PV Gas Son My LNG import terminal approval.
gogpt_prior_assessment: GOGPT's 'Son My I power station' (2,250 MW, tier B, 0 km) is one of the two plants this terminal supplies (direction test), not a captive plant belonging to the terminal.
